rows.note: Use this as the all-purpose choice for fastening or securing someone or something with a strap or similar tie.

example.english: I used a rope to strap the mat to the roof of the car.
example.traditional: 我用繩將張蓆綁喺架車頂。
example.jyutping: ngo5 jung6 sing4 zoeng1 zoeng1 zik6 bong2 hai2 gaa3 ce1 deng2

rows.note: Use this when the strap is fastened by engaging a buckle, especially for a seat belt or similar restraint.

example.english: Remember to strap on your seat belt when you get in the car.
example.jyutping: soeng5 ce1 gei3 dak1 kau3 on1 cyun4 daai2

rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice for a narrow flexible strip used to tie, fasten, or carry something.

example.english: The strap came loose, and the bag fell to the ground.
example.traditional: 條帶甩咗，個袋跌咗落地。
example.jyutping: tiu4 daai2 lat1 zo2 go3 doi2 dit3 zo2 lok6 dei6

rows.note: Use this specifically when the strap is worn on or rests on the shoulder.

example.english: The shoulder strap on this bag is too long and keeps slipping off my shoulder.
example.traditional: 呢個袋嘅肩帶太長，成日跣落膊頭。
example.jyutping: ni1 go3 doi2 ge3 gin1 daai3 taai3 coeng4 seng4 jat6 sin2 lok6 bok3 tau4

rows.note: Use this for the firearm slang sense; Cantonese normally uses the ordinary word 槍 rather than a special slang equivalent.

example.english: They heard that guy was carrying a strap, so everyone took off.
example.traditional: 聽講嗰條友身上有槍，大家即刻散水。
example.jyutping: teng1 gong2 go2 tiu4 jau2 san1 soeng6 jau5 coeng1 daai6 gaa1 zik1 hak1 saan3 seoi2
